settings.gapPenaltyDescription: How confident a match must be to beat leaving both sentences unaligned. Higher values reject more weak matches — useful when front matter, credits, or other boilerplate with no real counterpart ends up glued to unrelated real sentences. Lower values allow more (sometimes weaker but correct) matches through.

hero.description: A free and open-source, fully in-browser tool for creating parallel texts from two books in different languages — no accounts, no uploads, no Python.
hero.imageAlt: ParallelTexts side-by-side view of Alice in Wonderland in Japanese and English

whatIsIt.title: What is it?
whatIsIt.p1: ParallelTexts takes two versions of the same book — one in your native language, one in the language you are learning — and automatically aligns their sentences so you can read them side by side, sentence by sentence.
whatIsIt.p2: The output is a <bold>parallel corpus</bold>: a structured list of sentence pairs where each source sentence is matched to its translation. You can read it directly in the browser as a paginated ebook-style view, or export it for use in other tools.

whoIsItFor.title: Who is it for?
whoIsItFor.learners: <bold>Language learners</bold> who want to read a novel in a foreign language with a trusted translation always one tap away.
whoIsItFor.linguists: <bold>Linguists and translators</bold> who need to build small parallel corpora quickly, without setting up a pipeline.
whoIsItFor.researchers: <bold>Researchers</bold> looking for a lightweight, reproducible alignment tool that runs entirely on their own machine.
whoIsItFor.footer: The tool is designed to be approachable to anyone — no command-line knowledge required.

howItWorks.title: How does the alignment work?
howItWorks.intro: Under the hood, ParallelTexts runs a three-stage ML pipeline — entirely inside your browser using WebAssembly:
howItWorks.step1: <bold>1. Sentence splitting</bold> — Each book is split into individual sentences.
howItWorks.step2: <bold>2. Multilingual embedding</bold> — Every sentence is converted to a vector (a list of numbers that captures its meaning) using a multilingual AI model. Because the model understands 50+ languages at once, semantically equivalent sentences in different languages end up with similar vectors.
howItWorks.step3: <bold>3. Needleman–Wunsch alignment</bold> — A dynamic-programming algorithm (the same family used in DNA sequence alignment) finds the globally optimal pairing of source and target sentences based on their vector similarity.
howItWorks.outro: The result is a list of aligned pairs tagged as 1:1 matches, or source/target gaps where no counterpart was found.

modelDownload.title: The model download
modelDownload.p1: The AI model (~500 MB–1.1 GB depending on which you choose) is downloaded once from the Hugging Face model hub and then cached permanently in your browser. Subsequent alignments reuse the cached version — no re-download needed.
modelDownload.p2: Alignment is compute-intensive. A dedicated GPU is highly recommended — it can be 10–20× faster than running on CPU alone. Browsers with WebGPU support (Chrome 113+, Edge) will use your GPU automatically; others fall back to WebAssembly on the CPU.
modelDownload.p3: You can manage which models are cached from the <settingsLink>Settings page</settingsLink>.

formats.title: Supported file formats
formats.epub: <bold>EPUB</bold> — full support including cover art and chapter structure.
formats.pdf: <bold>PDF</bold> — text extraction via PDF.js (quality depends on the PDF).
formats.furigana: Japanese EPUBs are preprocessed to strip furigana before alignment so that phonetic readings do not interfere with the embeddings.

reading.title: Reading your alignment
reading.intro: After alignment completes you get two reading modes:
reading.popover: <bold>Popover view</bold> — Read the source text as a paginated ebook. Tap any sentence to see its aligned translation in a popover.
reading.sideBySide: <bold>Side-by-side view</bold> — Both languages displayed in parallel columns, every sentence pair on the same row.
reading.exportIntro: You can also export any alignment in two formats:
reading.epub: <bold>EPUB</bold> — a fully readable parallel ebook. Source sentences are shown by default; click any entry to reveal its translation. Images from the original books are preserved. The EPUB also embeds a hidden manifest so it can be imported back into ParallelTexts with the full alignment intact (see below).
reading.tsv: <bold>TSV</bold> — a tab-separated file with one sentence pair per row and an optional confidence score in the third column. Gap rows are preserved with an empty cell on the missing side. Any 2- or 3-column TSV works on import — not just files from ParallelTexts.
reading.importBack: Both formats can be <bold>imported back</bold> into ParallelTexts from the <alignmentsLink>Alignments page</alignmentsLink>. Importing a ParallelTexts-exported EPUB restores the alignment exactly — pairs, images, and metadata — with no need to re-run the AI model. Importing the same EPUB as a <bold>book</bold> (on the <booksLink>Books page</booksLink>) shows only the source text, making it usable as a standalone foreign-language book.
